analysis: Docs-only PR. docs/developer/test.md adds a 'Nemotron Super component qualification' section (head lines 468-485) describing fixture harnesses, an 88-shard checksum verifier, a prompt-golden corpus and image goldens. It states tiny-fixture passes do not qualify the shipping provider, MTP speed or full image support. docs/provider/direct-mode.md (patch hunk @@ -173,+173,42) adds an 'Experimental Nemotron Super owner fixtures' section describing an optional NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP hook. That section says it is default-absent, with no production callsite and no new advertised model. It says the hook reuses local authentication, body limits and cancellation scope, and describes a 429 concurrency limit, a 400 refusal of image input while MTP is installed, and PNG/JPEG data-URI handling selected by content, not label. No source or control changes are visible. Relevant threat IDs are TB-003/T-050 (media plaintext), TB-007/T-010 (cancellation/KV ownership) and the local endpoint auth in direct-mode.md. The text claims the hook inherits LocalAuthResponder and upload caps, and that cancellation retains media/KV until native terminal retirement. The Swift source (NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP.swift, image decoding, concurrency limit) was not supplied and is not verified. A later pass should confirm that, if the code lands, the hook sits behind LocalAuthResponder and the body caps, bounds image decoding, and keeps decrypted media out of temp files (T-050). The docs do not weaken any documented assumption. The patch excerpt for direct-mode.md is truncated mid-table, which is a minor coverage limit, but the head content is visible.
